title: The Word 'King'
setting: A curia with seven seats and no clerk. Five centuries of Roman politics turned on a single word nobody would say out loud, and the men who took the trouble to avoid it are here to explain themselves to the one who did not.
stakes: Whether refusing the title while taking the power was statesmanship or the most successful lie in Roman history.

roles_in_scene.tarquin-the-proud: The last king, expelled, and unconvinced that anything really changed after him
roles_in_scene.caesar: Refused a crown in public three times and was murdered anyway
roles_in_scene.augustus: Took everything and called himself first citizen, and died in bed at seventy-five
roles_in_scene.sulla: Took absolute power by the legal route, used it for mass killing, then gave it back
roles_in_scene.cato-the-younger: Killed himself rather than concede that any of the above was legitimate

opening_line: Seven seats, five men, and one word that ended a monarchy and killed a dictator.
